question: Worst-case first tokens after a controlled page-cache drop (POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED) on ps-iq2xxs vs warm, within 40/28 budgets
method: Sustained-decode harness lineage + --cold-cache flag (7d14cc14): whole-file POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED on the 75,216,526,912-byte GGUF via read-only fd, requested AFTER the Tier A guard and BEFORE the dry check/scope launch; identical config both arms (ps-iq2xxs, nmax4/DRAFT1, seed42/temp0, 68-token prompt, 2x256 decode, cache_prompt false); only the fadvise differs (cold_cache summary flag + cache_drop record). Binary SHA 3235529f... unchanged.
honest_reading: The fadvise call completed on the exact file and byte count, and the cold arm stayed within every budget.

BUT the cold state was NOT verified (no mincore residency snapshot before load): DONTNEED is advisory, the loader mmaps and may fault only a subset, and other same-day runs left the host page cache rich. The load-to-ready delta is 36 s vs 32 s (4 s, ~12%) and first-request decode 35.5 vs 43.6 tok/s (~19% slower).

Therefore this is evidence of a bounded worst-case-behavior under an advisory drop, NOT proof of a fully cold load. A future slice can add the mincore residency check (scripts/expert_bw_calib.py lineage) before the launcher to prove coldness.
Key practical result stands: even the slower cold-arm request is 35.5 tok/s — far above the 20 tok/s floor.
limitations: n=1 per arm, single prompt, same-day host state
no NVMe bandwidth measurement in this slice
warm arm ran second; host state evolved slightly between arms (4.5 min apart)
